incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty HIGH: Multiple cudaMalloc OOMs detected in pool g-rt-emb-v2 (embeddings) — alert rate 120/min. 23 nodes reporting CUBLAS/CUDA alloc failures. Affected services: ACME_Corp-embeddings, payroll-service-prod. Auto-shedder triggered evictions.

alex: Acked. I'm live on this pager. Adding olivia for T2. Starting triage — do we have any deploys in the last 30m?

olivia: grabbing logs now. No deploys in the last 40m from deploy-bot. Autoscaler shows a rapid scale-down event ~4m ago then a burst of requests.

incident-bot: System note: autoscaler scaled g-rt-emb-v2 from 48 -> 36 at 00:12:03 UTC, then scale attempts blocked due to GPU allocation failures. KVCache reclaim events: >500/min on those nodes.

miguel: quick glance at stack traces — reclaim loop seems to be thrashing and leaving fragmented device memory. Logs show repeated: 

```
2026-02-11T00:16:17Z inferencerd[pid=8421]: cudaMalloc failed: CUBLAS_ALLOC_FAILED (out of memory)
2026-02-11T00:16:17Z kvcache: reclaim: scanned=1048576 freed=0 fragmentation=0.87
2026-02-11T00:16:18Z inferencerd[pid=8421]: kernel: cudnn conv fallback -> CPU (latency spike)
```

miguel: TL;DR: kvcache reclaim is failing to free contiguous blocks; `cudaMalloc` fails and we see fallback to CPU that will spike latency. Not a model change.

ryan: I can drain 3 worst nodes from that pool and restart inferencerd to force memory compaction. Suggest: mark node[g-rt-emb-v2-eu-07..09] unsched, wait for in-flight to drain, then restart. Command I will run:

```
# mark nodes unsched
infractl node cordon g-rt-emb-v2-eu-07
infractl node cordon g-rt-emb-v2-eu-08
infractl node cordon g-rt-emb-v2-eu-09
# restart inferencerd service
infractl ssh g-rt-emb-v2-eu-07 -- systemctl restart inferencerd
```

alex: go ahead. Meanwhile flip routing for ACME embeds to fallback-small-quant (lower memory) and throttle batch_size to 1 for the pool. That should reduce new OOMs.

linda: support: ACME_Corp has flagged rising 5xxs from embeddings API; creating a high-priority incident note and outbound comms draft. ETA for first customer update 00:40 UTC.

pagerduty: Escalation: If no ack in 3 minutes, notify oncall-2. (Alex already acked).

ryan: cordoned nodes and restarted inferencerd on the 3 nodes. Observed immediate reconnects but a couple of pods failed to reclaim. Running `inferencerd --gc-kvcache` on those nodes now.

```
# manual GC trigger
infractl ssh g-rt-emb-v2-eu-07 -- /usr/local/bin/inferencerd --gc-kvcache --force
```

miguel: after GC we see cudaMalloc success on those nodes. KV free counts increased. However kv hit ratio dropped ~72% -> 18%, so embedding latency is higher while caches repopulate. We'll monitor.

alex: routing flip in place: ACME -> fallback-small-quant, batch_size=1. Throttling applied to payroll-service-prod (reduce concurrency to 4).

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Alert rate down to baseline (5/min). OOMs within pool g-rt-emb-v2 stopped after restarts/GC. Autoscaler now reporting stable capacity 44 nodes.

miguel: one follow-up — there's evidence of kvcache fragmentation caused by a long-lived pin from an older quantized loader on a subset of nodes. We'll schedule a targeted image bump that fixes the allocator behavior. Creating a CL.

olivia: adding action items: 1) postmortem (owner: alex), 2) change: add periodic `/gc-kvcache` healthcheck if fragmentation > 0.8, 3) runbook update for draining + GC sequence.

alex: handing over to olivia for remainder of oncall window. I'll create the postmortem ticket and include customer impact timeline. Linda, please send the ACME update: what happened, mitigations, next steps.

linda: outbound sent (subject: ACME embeddings degraded). Support note includes degraded latency, fallbacks, mitigation steps taken, and ETA for next update.

incident-bot: Note: PagerDuty incident closed by alex at 00:37 UTC. Please use `#postmortems` for follow-up discussion.

alex: Thanks team. Summary: Root cause — KV cache fragmentation preventing contiguous device allocations -> cudaMalloc OOM -> inferencerd fallback -> customer 5xxs. Mitigation — drain/restart worst nodes, run GC, throttle/reroute heavy customers, deploy allocator fix.

olivia: taking ownership for the follow-ups and postmortem. Marking this thread resolved for oncall. :white_check_mark:
